Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 97, verses 1–5:

Explanation of the words:

Inna anzalnahu (Indeed, We revealed it): That is, the Qur'an was sent down all at once from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the lowest heaven (sama' al-dunya).

Fi laylat al-qadr (On the Night of Decree): That is, the night of judgment and determination, in which the affairs of the whole year are decreed.

Wa ma adraka ma laylat al-qadr (And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is?): That is, its matter is great.

Laylat al-qadr khayrun min alfi shahr (The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months): That is, righteous deeds in it, such as prayer, recitation of the Qur'an, and supplication, are better than worship of a thousand months that do not include the Night of Decree, and that is eighty-three years and four months.

Wa al-ruh fiha (And the angels descend in it, along with the Spirit): That is, Jibril, on the Night of Decree.

Bi idhni rabbihim (By the permission of their Lord): That is, they descend by His command, may He be exalted, to them for the sending down in it.

Min kulli amr (With every decree): That is, with every matter that Allah decreed in that year, of provision, term of life, and other things.

Salamun hiya hatta matli' al-fajr (Peace it is until the rising of the dawn): That is, it is peace from all evil, from the sunset until the break of dawn.

Explanation of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, We sent it down﴾, mean the noble Qur'an, which the deniers denied and the disbelievers rejected. Allah, the Exalted, informs that what His servant and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) recites is the truth, the revelation of Allah and His Book, which He sent down all at once from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, on the night of judgment and decree, in which Allah decides what He wills of the events of the world, of provision, term of life, and other things, until the beginning of the coming year; and this occurs every year. This is like His saying, ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were ever warning. Therein is made distinct every precise matter﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 3-4]. For what Allah decreed and ordained to exist has been written in the Preserved Tablet, and among it is the Noble Qur'an. Then on the Night of Decree a copy of the events of the year is taken and given to the angels, and it is executed literally during that year. Therefore the Night of Decree, in the sense of determination, has great significance, and Allah preferred it over a thousand months and informed of the reason for its excellence: the angels descend in it, and Jibril with them, by the permission of their Lord, that is, they descend by Allah's permission to them and His command to them to descend. They descend accompanied by every decree that Allah decreed and ordained in that year, of good and evil, of provision and term of life. Because of the excellence of this night, worship in it surpasses its like by manifold multiplication, for the deed of that night is reckoned to its doer as the deed of a thousand nights, that is, eighty-three years and four months. This is what is indicated by the saying of the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months. The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord with every matter﴾, and His saying, ﴿Peace it is until the rising of the dawn﴾, that is, it is peace from every evil, for all of it is good from sunset until the break of its dawn. All of it is peace: the peace of the angels upon the worshipping believing men and women, and safety from every evil. And praise be to Allah who made us among its people.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of revelation and establishment of Muhammadan prophethood.

2- Affirmation of the creed of qada' and qadar (divine decree and predestination).

3- The excellence of the Night of Decree and the excellence of worship in it.

4- Clarification that the Qur'an was sent down in Ramadan all at once from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, and that its revelation to the Messenger (ﷺ) also began in Ramadan.

5- Encouragement to seek the Night of Decree to win its excellence, and that is in the last ten nights of Ramadan; the most hoped-for night within the last ten is an odd night, such as the twenty-first through the twenty-ninth, based on the authentic hadith, "Seek it in the last ten nights." 6- Recommendation to increase recitation and listening to the Qur'an in it, because Jibril used to review the Qur'an with the Messenger (ﷺ) twice in Ramadan.
